# openmetadata_table (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata table. A table belongs to a database schema and owns the ordered list of columns that describe its shape.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_database_service" "warehouse" {
  name         = "warehouse"
  service_type = "Postgres"
}

resource "openmetadata_database" "analytics" {
  name    = "analytics"
  service = openmetadata_database_service.warehouse.name
}

resource "openmetadata_database_schema" "public" {
  name     = "public"
  database = openmetadata_database.analytics.fully_qualified_name
}

resource "openmetadata_table" "users" {
  name            = "users"
  database_schema = openmetadata_database_schema.public.fully_qualified_name
  display_name    = "Users"
  description     = "One row per registered user."

  columns = [
    {
      name             = "id"
      data_type        = "BIGINT"
      description      = "Primary key."
      ordinal_position = 1
    },
    {
      name             = "email"
      data_type        = "VARCHAR"
      data_length      = 255
      ordinal_position = 2
    },
    {
      name             = "created_at"
      data_type        = "TIMESTAMP"
      ordinal_position = 3
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `columns` (Attributes List) Ordered columns of the table. Replacing the list sends the whole column set through a single JSON Patch operation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns))
- `database_schema` (String) Fully qualified name of the parent database schema, in the form service.database.schema. Changing it replaces the table.
- `name` (String) Table name. Changing it replaces the table, because the name is part of its fully qualified name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the table.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name, in the form service.database.schema.table.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

<a id="nestedatt--columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `columns`

Required:

- `data_type` (String) OpenMetadata column data type, for example VARCHAR, BIGINT or TIMESTAMP.
- `name` (String) Column name.

Optional:

- `data_length` (Number) Length for CHAR, VARCHAR, BINARY and VARBINARY columns. The server requires it for those types.
- `description` (String) Markdown description of the column.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable column name.
- `ordinal_position` (Number) One-based position of the column. Filled by the server when omitted.
- `precision` (Number) Numeric precision for DECIMAL and NUMERIC columns.
- `scale` (Number) Numeric scale.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_table.users 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, in the form service.database.schema.table.
terraform import openmetadata_table.users warehouse.analytics.public.users
```
